description: Authoritative Ground Control Point (GCP) audit fixture for Herman Moll 1715 map (LOC gm71005442).

canonical_gcps.name: Havana, Cuba
canonical_gcps.pinpoint_rationale: Castillo del Morro promontory guarding the narrow entrance channel to Havana harbor, south of Bahia Honda on the northwest Cuban coast.

canonical_gcps.name: Port Royal, Jamaica
canonical_gcps.pinpoint_rationale: The tip of the Palisadoes sand spit enclosing Kingston Harbour and Port Royal on the south coast of Jamaica, distinctly engraved with anchorage anchor.

canonical_gcps.name: Veracruz, Mexico
canonical_gcps.feature: San Juan de Ulua island fort
canonical_gcps.pinpoint_rationale: Island fortress of San Juan de Ulua directly offshore from the port of Veracruz on the southwestern Gulf coast of New Spain.

canonical_gcps.name: Cartagena, Colombia
canonical_gcps.pinpoint_rationale: Harbor entrance at Boca Chica and fortress symbol defending Cartagena bay on the Tierra Firme coast. Pinpointed from coastal engraving, correcting previous draft offset.

canonical_gcps.name: Portobelo, Panama
canonical_gcps.pinpoint_rationale: Embayment of Portobelo on the Caribbean coast of the Isthmus of Panama, just east of the mouth of Rio Chagres.

canonical_gcps.name: Saint Augustine, Florida
canonical_gcps.pinpoint_rationale: The coastal barrier island inlet and Castillo de San Marcos on the northeast coast of Florida. Preserved in Candidate C for Atlantic coastal continuity; excluded from F1 regional basin.

canonical_gcps.name: San Juan, Puerto Rico
canonical_gcps.pinpoint_rationale: The fortified islet and harbor entrance of San Juan on the north coast of Puerto Rico (San Juan Bautista).

canonical_gcps.name: Santo Domingo, Hispaniola
canonical_gcps.pinpoint_rationale: Mouth of the Ozama River on the south-central coast of Hispaniola (Santo Domingo).

canonical_gcps.name: Bridgetown, Barbados
canonical_gcps.pinpoint_rationale: Carlisle Bay anchorage on the southwest coast of Barbados, easternmost Windward island. Preserved in Candidate C to anchor Lesser Antilles; excluded from F1 regional basin.

canonical_gcps.name: Willemstad, Curacao
canonical_gcps.pinpoint_rationale: Deep natural inlet of Santa Anna Bay on the south coast of Curacao ('Bay St. Anna'), precisely pinpointed on the engraved harbor channel, correcting the 85px open-water error of earlier drafts.

canonical_gcps.name: Cabo San Antonio, Cuba
canonical_gcps.pinpoint_rationale: Prominent western cape of Cuba, serving as critical cartographic anchor between the Gulf of Mexico and Yucatan Channel.

canonical_gcps.name: Cabo Maisi, Cuba
canonical_gcps.pinpoint_rationale: Easternmost cape of Cuba framing the Windward Passage opposite Hispaniola.

canonical_gcps.name: Charles Town, South Carolina
canonical_gcps.pinpoint_rationale: Entrance to Charleston Harbor on the Atlantic seaboard, anchoring the northern neatline of the chart field. Excluded from F1 regional basin.

excluded_investigated_points.rejection_rationale: The physical engraving of Moll's 1715 map terminates at approximately 33°N latitude. Cape Hatteras (35°15'N) is physically off the top edge of the copperplate. In Packet 8, an arbitrary pixel at [2980, 740] (in the North Carolina coastal sounds near Beaufort) was assigned to Hatteras, injecting a >250 km systematic error that distorted the entire northern neatline under polynomial warping.

Bermuda is preserved unmasked in the main chart field. However, in Moll's 1715 engraving (as in contemporary early 18th-century cartography prior to marine chronometers), Bermuda was plotted ~250 km too far west relative to the North American coastline. Using it as an active affine control would distort the continental coastline and Greater Antilles.

excluded_investigated_points.feature_name: Mexico City ('The city of Mexico in New Spain')
excluded_investigated_points.rejection_rationale: The panoramic bird's-eye view of Mexico City is LOC Inset #6, engraved in the lower margin (y >= 2905). It is completely outside the main chart neatline crop (y <= 2895), requiring zero internal masking.

packet8_baseline_accounting.root_cause_defect: Packet 8 used 14 GCPs with several severe coordinate errors (including off-sheet Cape Hatteras and an uncalibrated coordinate frame). Second-order polynomial fitting ('gdalwarp -order 2') curled coordinate space between those flawed points, producing visible buckling along the Florida coast, Cuba, and neatlines.
